levels.title: Beginner (Acceso)
levels.milestone: Handle the present tense, gender and agreement, and get through a first day in Spain without English.
canDo: Read Spanish aloud correctly from the first week, and write the accents that carry meaning: hablo and habló, esta and está, si and sí.
Conjugate the present of the three regular conjugations plus ser, estar, haber and ir, and use the four irregular families querer, poder, pedir and the yo-form group.
Make articles and adjectives agree with their noun in gender and number, which is what holds a Spanish sentence together.
Choose between ser and estar, and between hay and está, in the ordinary cases.
Say what you like with gustar, what you want with querer, what you have to do with tener que, and what you are going to do with ir a.

descriptors: I can recognise familiar words and very basic phrases concerning myself, my family and immediate concrete surroundings when people speak slowly and clearly.
I can understand familiar names, words and very simple sentences, for example on notices and posters or in catalogues.
I can interact in a simple way provided the other person is prepared to repeat or rephrase things at a slower rate of speech and help me formulate what I am trying to say.
I can ask and answer simple questions in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics.
I can use simple phrases and sentences to describe where I live and people I know.
I can write a short simple postcard, for example sending holiday greetings.
I can fill in forms with personal details, for example entering my name, nationality and address on a hotel registration form.

exam.name: DELE A1
exam.description: The first rung of the official ladder. It is not required for anything legally, so treat it as a checkpoint rather than a destination: it proves the present tense and everyday survival language are solid before you commit to the level that is required. Four pruebas, twenty five points each, a hundred in total. Three of them are sat on the exam date and the speaking one may be held on the day before or after.
sections: Comprensión de lectura, 45 minutes, 4 tareas, 25 items
Expresión e interacción escritas, 25 minutes, 2 tareas
Expresión e interacción orales, 10 minutes plus 10 minutes of preparation, 3 tareas
exam.passRule: The four pruebas are scored out of 25 each and then paired into two groups. Grupo 1 is reading plus writing, Grupo 2 is listening plus speaking, and each group is worth 50 points. You are apto only if you score at least 30 of 50 in BOTH groups. That means a weak section can be carried by its partner inside the same group, but a weak group cannot be rescued by the other group, however well it went.

levels.title: Elementary (Plataforma)
levels.milestone: Tell a story in the past, give an instruction, and reach the level Spain's nationality procedure actually asks for.
canDo: Use the three past tenses and choose between them: he hablado for what still touches today, hablé for what is closed, hablaba for description and habit.
Use direct and indirect object pronouns, combine them, and handle le turning into se before lo and la.
Give instructions and directions with the affirmative imperative in tú, vosotros, usted and ustedes, with the pronouns attached.
Compare things with más que, menos que and tan como, and modify with adverbs in -mente.
Write a personal email, note or postcard of sixty to seventy words in reply to a message, which is the DELE A2 writing task exactly.

descriptors: I can understand phrases and the highest frequency vocabulary related to areas of most immediate personal relevance, for example very basic personal and family information, shopping, local area, employment.
I can catch the main point in short, clear, simple messages and announcements.
I can read very short, simple texts.
I can find specific, predictable information in simple everyday material such as advertisements, prospectuses, menus and timetables, and I can understand short simple personal letters.
I can communicate in simple and routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar topics and activities.
I can handle very short social exchanges, even though I cannot usually understand enough to keep the conversation going myself.
I can use a series of phrases and sentences to describe in simple terms my family and other people, living conditions, my educational background and my present or most recent job.
I can write short, simple notes and messages relating to matters in areas of immediate need.
I can write a very simple personal letter, for example thanking someone for something.

exam.name: DELE A2
exam.description: The level that carries legal weight in Spain: a DELE at A2 or above is what the nationality by residence procedure requires from applicants whose first language is not Spanish, alongside a separate civics test that examines knowledge of the country rather than the language and which this course does not prepare. Nationals of the Spanish-speaking countries are exempt from the language exam but not from the civics one. Four pruebas, twenty five points each. Notice that A2 gives you the same twenty five items in reading as A1 but nearly twice the reading time and much longer texts.
sections: Comprensión de lectura, 60 minutes, 4 tareas, 25 items
Expresión e interacción escritas, 45 minutes, 2 tareas
Expresión e interacción orales, 12 minutes plus 12 minutes of preparation, 3 tareas
exam.passRule: The same grouped rule as every DELE from A1 to C1. Grupo 1 is reading plus writing and Grupo 2 is listening plus speaking, 50 points each, and apto requires at least 30 of 50 in BOTH groups. Sixty percent overall is not enough on its own: fifty in one group and ten in the other averages to the same sixty and still fails.

levels.title: Intermediate (Umbral)
levels.milestone: Use the subjunctive where Spanish demands it, argue a position, and pass the DELE B1.
canDo: Use the future and the conditional, which share one set of irregular stems, for prediction, probability, politeness and advice.
Form the present subjunctive and use it after wanting, doubting, valuing, and in purpose, time and concession clauses.
Give negative orders, which are the subjunctive in disguise, and place pronouns correctly on both sides of the imperative.
Report what someone said with the tense shift, and connect an argument with sin embargo, por lo tanto, aunque and ya que.
Write the two DELE B1 texts to length: an informal message of 100 to 120 words and a composition with an opinion of 130 to 150 words.

descriptors: I can understand the main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure and so on.
I can understand the main point of many radio or TV programmes on current affairs or topics of personal or professional interest when the delivery is relatively slow and clear.
I can understand texts that consist mainly of high frequency everyday or job-related language.
I can understand the description of events, feelings and wishes in personal letters.
I can deal with most situations likely to arise whilst travelling in an area where the language is spoken.
I can enter unprepared into conversation on topics that are familiar, of personal interest or pertinent to everyday life, for example family, hobbies, work, travel and current events.
I can connect phrases in a simple way in order to describe experiences and events, my dreams, hopes and ambitions.
I can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans, and narrate the plot of a book or film and describe my reactions.
I can write simple connected text on topics which are familiar or of personal interest.
I can write personal letters describing experiences and impressions.

exam.name: DELE B1
exam.description: The finish line of this course. B1 is above what Spanish nationality requires, and that is deliberate: A2 is a narrow place to stop, and B1 is the level that actually opens work and study, so the course carries you past the legal bar rather than to it. B1 is where the exam grows: reading and listening go from four tareas to five and from 25 items to 30 each, and the speaking prueba adds a fourth task. It is also where the input texts stop being peninsular only and start drawing on every variety of Spanish, which is why the second half of this course trains your ear on American accents as well.
sections: Comprensión de lectura, 70 minutes, 5 tareas, 30 items
Expresión e interacción escritas, 60 minutes, 2 tareas
Expresión e interacción orales, 15 minutes plus 15 minutes of preparation, 4 tareas
exam.passRule: Grupo 1 is reading plus writing and Grupo 2 is listening plus speaking, 50 points each, and apto requires at least 30 of 50 in BOTH groups. There is no minimum on any individual prueba, so a bad section is survivable if its partner is strong, but a bad group is not survivable at all.
